opp_007:n1.prompt:
You are helping me provision a new Google Workspace user account as part of onboarding a new hire. This step requires explicit human approval before any changes are applied to our workspace directory, so your job is to PREPARE everything needed and then stop.

First, ask me for any of the following details you don't already have:
- New hire's full name
- Desired primary email address (or naming convention to derive it, e.g. first.last@domain)
- Job title / department
- Manager or reporting line (if relevant to profile fields)
- Our Google Workspace primary domain
- Organizational unit (OU) the account should belong to, if we use OUs
- Any required profile fields (phone number, employee ID, location, etc.)

Once you have these, prepare a clear, complete draft of the new user account to be created in Google Workspace via the admin console (https://admin.google.com/), including: full name, proposed email address, organizational unit, job title, and any other profile fields I've provided. Present this as a checklist or summary I can review line by line.

Do not create, submit, or apply the account in Google Workspace yourself. Do not log in and perform the creation action. Your role is limited to drafting and organizing the exact values that will be entered, and flagging anything ambiguous or missing (e.g., conflicting email naming conventions, missing OU).

When the draft is complete, present it to me for review and explicitly stop for human sign-off — do not proceed to create the account until I confirm.

Report back with: the full draft of the proposed user account (all fields), any open questions or missing information, and a note confirming you are pausing for my approval before any account is created in Google Workspace.

opp_007:n2.prompt:
You are helping me finish provisioning a Google Workspace account for a new hire by adding them to the correct groups and shared drives. If you don't already have these, ask me for: (1) my Google Workspace domain, (2) the new hire's full workspace email address, (3) their team/department and role, (4) the specific Google Groups they should join (e.g., team distribution lists, all-staff, engineering-eng@ etc.), and (5) the shared drives they need access to along with the appropriate permission level for each (viewer, commenter, content manager, or manager).

Once you have this information, using my configured credentials with admin access to Google Workspace:
1. Add the user's email to each specified Google Group, matching standard onboarding conventions for their team/department if I haven't listed every group explicitly.
2. Add the user to each specified shared drive with the correct permission level.
3. Verify the additions by checking group membership and shared drive member lists to confirm the user now appears correctly in each.

If any group or shared drive name is ambiguous or doesn't exist, stop and ask me to clarify rather than guessing or creating new groups/drives.

When done, report back a concise summary listing: the user's email, every group they were added to, every shared drive they were added to with the permission level granted, and confirmation that each addition was verified. Flag any groups or drives you could not add them to and why.

opp_007:n3.prompt:
You are helping me provision app access for a new hire via our identity provider setup in {{vendor}}, as part of onboarding. If you don't already have them, ask me for: the new hire's full name and work email, which organization/tenant they belong to, the app(s) or group(s) they need access to, and confirmation that our {{vendor}} account has SSO/SCIM already configured with our IdP (e.g., Okta, Entra, or Google Workspace).

Once you have this, please:
1. Confirm the {{vendor}} SSO connection for our organization is active and the relevant verified domain is in place; if not, flag this before proceeding.
2. Check whether SCIM sync is enabled for our directory in {{vendor}} so that new users are pulled in automatically, or whether the user needs to be added manually via just-in-time provisioning on first login.
3. Add or confirm the new hire's membership in the correct organization/tenant in {{vendor}}, assigning them to the appropriate groups or roles that map to the apps they need.
4. If an invitation flow is required (rather than SCIM auto-sync), prepare the invitation with the correct email, organization, and role/group assignment, but do not send it if that action requires elevated approval — check whether sending requires sign-off.
5. Verify that deprovisioning is correctly wired: confirm that removing this user from the IdP or its groups will revoke their access in {{vendor}} via SCIM, so we have one clean offboarding path.

Use your configured credentials to access the {{vendor}} dashboard or API — do not ask me for or handle any tokens, passwords, or secrets directly.

Done looks like: the new hire has an active or pending membership in the correct organization with correct group/role assignments, SSO and SCIM sync are confirmed functional, and any required invitation is drafted and ready.

Report back with: what was configured, current status (active/pending), any gaps found (e.g., SCIM not enabled, domain not verified), and anything that needs my attention or approval before going further.

opp_007:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the final step of provisioning a workspace account for a new hire: their first sign-in and MFA enrollment. This step cannot be completed by you or me — the new hire must personally authenticate and bind their own device, per our security policy. Your job is to prepare everything needed so the new hire can do this smoothly, then stop.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: the new hire's full name, their new workspace email address, the temporary password or sign-in method already set up for their account, our workspace provider (e.g., Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Okta, etc.), and our organization's MFA policy details (which factors are allowed — authenticator app, SMS, hardware key, etc.).

Then prepare:
1. A clear, step-by-step written guide for the new hire covering: how to navigate to the sign-in page, how to log in with their temporary credentials, how to set a new password if required, and how to enroll in MFA using an approved method.
2. A short welcome message/email draft I can send them containing their workspace email, temporary credentials reference (without including the actual secret), and the enrollment guide.
3. A checklist for me to confirm before sending: correct email address, temporary password already generated and ready to hand off securely, MFA policy confirmed, and IT/security contact info included in case the new hire needs help.

Do not attempt to sign in, enter credentials, or enroll MFA on the new hire's behalf — this remains a human step that only the new hire can complete on their own device. Once your guide, message draft, and checklist are ready, present them to me and stop for human sign-off before anything is sent or the new hire is asked to proceed.
